The constraints force a unique schedule. Elif, Ben and Ivo must sit consecutively, and Gus is directly before Elif, Finn directly before Gus. So Finn, Gus, Elif, Ben, Ivo form a fixed five-slot block starting at slot p. Exactly one person between Elif and Finn fits this block.

- **p = 2 or 3** fail. With p = 2, slot 1 can only hold Cara or Dev, but neither can be paired with an adjacent partner. With p = 3, Hana must be in slot 9, which leaves no room for Cara and Dev to sit together while Dev still comes after Gus.
- **p = 1** works only with Cara in 6, Dev in 7, Hana in 8, Ann in 9. Every other arrangement of slots 6 to 9 breaks the Ann–Cara gap or the Ben–Hana gap.

Check of the result: Finn(1) Gus(2) Elif(3) Ben(4) Ivo(5) Cara(6) Dev(7) Hana(8) Ann(9). Ben is before Hana by 4 slots. Ivo is right after Ben, Ben is right after Elif, Gus is right after Finn, Elif is right after Gus, and Dev is right after Cara. Exactly one person (Gus) sits between Elif and Finn. Gus (2) is before Dev (7). Ivo (5) and Elif (3) are before Ann (9). Ann and Cara are 3 apart.
